reason: The picture shows blood approaching the kidney filter, so this directly starts the filtering goal.
expectation: Small substances should pass through the filter while blood cells and large proteins stay in the blood.

effect: The filter lets useful glucose and water through along with wastes, so the recovery tube is needed next.
reaction: It is interesting that filtering does not separate out just the waste.
reason: The recovery tube's picture shows useful substances moving back toward the blood.
expectation: The tube should return glucose, some salts and much of the water to the blood.

effect: Useful substances returned to the blood, and the remaining waste-containing fluid still needs a route to the bladder.
reaction: The two-stage process makes more sense now.
reason: The ureters are shown leading from the kidneys toward the bladder, so they should start the drainage route.
expectation: The ureters should attach to the kidneys' marked drainage outlets.

effect: The ureters are attached to the kidney outlets; the bladder still needs to be fitted.
reaction: The downward route is clear now.
reason: The bladder is the remaining named slot, and the ureters lead toward it.
expectation: The bladder should connect to the ureters, completing the drainage route.

effect: The kidneys now have a continuous route through the ureters to the bladder; the remaining fluid still needs to be collected.
reaction: Seeing the whole route connected is satisfying.
reason: The remaining fluid contains wastes, and the completed kidney route leads to the bladder.
expectation: The remaining fluid should travel through the ureters and collect as urine in the bladder.

effect: The remaining fluid reached the bladder as urine, completing the collection goal.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the filtering and drainage routes come together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Recovering useful substances after filtering was most worthwhile: it showed why the kidney cannot simply filter out waste.

leastWorthwhile.text: Attaching the ureters and bladder was straightforward and a little repetitive, though it made the route clear.

surprise.text: I was surprised that useful glucose and water pass through the filter along with wastes and must be recovered.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the pictures and named slots explained the pairings.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: seeing a familiar organ work as a connected process was interesting, especially the recovery step.
